  float *dx;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&dx, input_bytes);
  cudaMemcpy(dx, x, input_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

  float *dy;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&dy, input_bytes);
  cudaMemcpy(dy, y, input_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

  float *df;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&df, output_float_bytes);

  int *di;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&di, output_int_bytes);

  short *ds;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&ds, output_short_bytes);

  dim3 grids (n / 256 + 1);
  dim3 blocks (256);

  printf("\n======== output type is f32 ========\n");
  auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++)
    compute_f <<<grids, blocks>>> (n, dy, dx, df);
  cudaDeviceSynchronize();

  auto end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  auto time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average execution time: %f (us)\n", (time * 1e-3f) / repeat);

  cudaMemcpy(hf, df, output_float_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  reference_f (n, y, x, rf);
  float error = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (fabsf(rf[i] - hf[i]) > 1e-3f) {
      error += (ri[i] - hi[i]) * (ri[i] - hi[i]);
    }
  }
  printf("RMSE: %f\n", sqrtf(error / n));

  printf("\n======== output type is i32 ========\n");

  start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++)
    compute_i <<<grids, blocks>>> (n, dy, dx, di);
  cudaDeviceSynchronize();

  end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average execution time: %f (us)\n", (time * 1e-3f) / repeat);

  cudaMemcpy(hi, di, output_int_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  reference_i (n, y, x, ri);
  error = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (abs(ri[i] - hi[i]) > 0) {
      error += (ri[i] - hi[i]) * (ri[i] - hi[i]);
    }
  }

  error = 0;
  reference_s (n, y, x, rs);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (abs(rs[i] - hs[i]) > 0) {
      error += (rs[i] - hs[i]) * (rs[i] - hs[i]);
    }
  }

  cudaFree(di);
  cudaFree(ds);
  cudaFree(dx);
  cudaFree(dy);
  free(x);
  free(y);
  free(hf);
  free(hi);
  free(hs);
  free(rf);

  free(rs);

__global__
void compute_f (const int n,
                const float *x,
                const float *y,
                      float *r)
{
  const int i = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  if (i >= n) return;
  const float vy = y[i];
  const float vx = x[i];
  r[i] = safe_atan2f< 3>(vy, vx) +
         safe_atan2f< 5>(vy, vx) +
         safe_atan2f< 7>(vy, vx) +
         safe_atan2f< 9>(vy, vx) +
         safe_atan2f<11>(vy, vx) +
         safe_atan2f<13>(vy, vx) +
         safe_atan2f<15>(vy, vx);
}

__global__
void compute_s (const int n,
                const float *x,
                const float *y,
                      short *r)
{
  const int i = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  if (i >= n) return;
  const float vy = y[i];
  const float vx = x[i];
  r[i] = unsafe_atan2s< 3>(vy, vx) +
         unsafe_atan2s< 5>(vy, vx) +
         unsafe_atan2s< 7>(vy, vx) +
         unsafe_atan2s< 9>(vy, vx);
}

__global__
void compute_i (const int n,
                const float *x,
                const float *y,
                      int *r)
{
  const int i = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  if (i >= n) return;
  const float vy = y[i];
  const float vx = x[i];
  r[i] = unsafe_atan2i< 3>(vy, vx) +
         unsafe_atan2i< 5>(vy, vx) +
         unsafe_atan2i< 7>(vy, vx) +
         unsafe_atan2i< 9>(vy, vx) +
         unsafe_atan2i<11>(vy, vx) +
         unsafe_atan2i<13>(vy, vx) +
         unsafe_atan2i<15>(vy, vx);
}

void reference_f (const int n,
                  const float *x,
                  const float *y,
                        float *r)
{
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const float vy = y[i];
    const float vx = x[i];
    r[i] = safe_atan2f< 3>(vy, vx) +
           safe_atan2f< 5>(vy, vx) +
           safe_atan2f< 7>(vy, vx) +
           safe_atan2f< 9>(vy, vx) +
           safe_atan2f<11>(vy, vx) +
           safe_atan2f<13>(vy, vx) +
           safe_atan2f<15>(vy, vx);
  }
}

void reference_s (const int n,
                  const float *x,
                  const float *y,
                        short *r)
{
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const float vy = y[i];
    const float vx = x[i];
    r[i] = unsafe_atan2s< 3>(vy, vx) +
           unsafe_atan2s< 5>(vy, vx) +

void reference_i (const int n,
                  const float *x,
                  const float *y,
                        int *r)
{
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const float vy = y[i];
    const float vx = x[i];
    r[i] = unsafe_atan2i< 3>(vy, vx) +
           unsafe_atan2i< 5>(vy, vx) +
           unsafe_atan2i< 7>(vy, vx) +
           unsafe_atan2i< 9>(vy, vx) +
           unsafe_atan2i<11>(vy, vx) +
           unsafe_atan2i<13>(vy, vx) +
           unsafe_atan2i<15>(vy, vx);
  }
}

int main(int argc, char* argv[])
{
  if (argc != 3) {
    printf("Usage: %s <number of coordinates> <repeat>\n", argv[0]);
    return 1;
  }
  const int n = atoi(argv[1]);
  const int repeat = atoi(argv[2]);
  const size_t input_bytes = sizeof(float) * n;
  const size_t output_float_bytes = sizeof(float) * n;
  const size_t output_int_bytes = sizeof(int) * n;
  const size_t output_short_bytes = sizeof(short) * n;

  float *x = (float*) malloc (input_bytes);
  float *y = (float*) malloc (input_bytes);

  float *hf = (float*) malloc (output_float_bytes);
    int *hi = (int*) malloc (output_int_bytes);
  short *hs = (short*) malloc (output_short_bytes);

  // reference
  float *rf = (float*) malloc (output_float_bytes);
    int *ri = (int*) malloc (output_int_bytes);
  short *rs = (short*) malloc (output_short_bytes);

  srand(123);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    x[i] = rand() / (float)RAND_MAX + 1.57f;
    y[i] = rand() / (float)RAND_MAX + 1.57f;
  }
  
  float *dx;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&dx, input_bytes);
  cudaMemcpy(dx, x, input_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

  float *dy;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&dy, input_bytes);
  cudaMemcpy(dy, y, input_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

  float *df;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&df, output_float_bytes);

  int *di;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&di, output_int_bytes);

  short *ds;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&ds, output_short_bytes);

  dim3 grids (n / 256 + 1);
  dim3 blocks (256);

  printf("\n======== output type is f32 ========\n");
  auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++)
    compute_f <<<grids, blocks>>> (n, dy, dx, df);
  cudaDeviceSynchronize();

  auto end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  auto time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average execution time: %f (us)\n", (time * 1e-3f) / repeat);

  cudaMemcpy(hf, df, output_float_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  reference_f (n, y, x, rf);
  float error = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (fabsf(rf[i] - hf[i]) > 1e-3f) {
      error += (ri[i] - hi[i]) * (ri[i] - hi[i]);
    }
  }
  printf("RMSE: %f\n", sqrtf(error / n));

  printf("\n======== output type is i32 ========\n");

  start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++)
    compute_i <<<grids, blocks>>> (n, dy, dx, di);
  cudaDeviceSynchronize();

  end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average execution time: %f (us)\n", (time * 1e-3f) / repeat);

  cudaMemcpy(hi, di, output_int_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  reference_i (n, y, x, ri);
  error = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (abs(ri[i] - hi[i]) > 0) {
      error += (ri[i] - hi[i]) * (ri[i] - hi[i]);
    }
  }
  printf("RMSE: %f\n", sqrtf(error / n));

  printf("\n======== output type is i16 ========\n");

  start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++)
    compute_s <<<grids, blocks>>> (n, dy, dx, ds);
  cudaDeviceSynchronize();

  end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average execution time: %f (us)\n", (time * 1e-3f) / repeat);

  cudaMemcpy(hs, ds, output_short_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  error = 0;
  reference_s (n, y, x, rs);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (abs(rs[i] - hs[i]) > 0) {
      error += (rs[i] - hs[i]) * (rs[i] - hs[i]);
    }
  }
  printf("RMSE: %f\n", sqrtf(error / n));

  cudaFree(df);
  cudaFree(di);
  cudaFree(ds);
  cudaFree(dx);
  cudaFree(dy);
  free(x);
  free(y);
  free(hf);
  free(hi);
  free(hs);
  free(rf);
  free(ri);
  free(rs);
  return 0;
}

### Write Traffic Amplification
- For streaming write patterns where the output footprint is larger than L2, actual DRAM write traffic can exceed the unique write footprint because of cache behavior and write-allocation effects.   constexpr short pi4 = short(maxshort / 4);
  constexpr short pi34 = short(3 * maxshort / 4);

  auto r = (std::abs(x) - std::abs(y)) / (std::abs(x) + std::abs(y));
  if (x < 0)
    r = -r;

  auto angle = (x >= 0) ? pi4 : pi34;
  angle += short(approx_atan2s_P<DEGREE>(r));

  return (y < 0) ? -angle : angle;
}

template <int DEGREE>
__device__ __host__
constexpr short unsafe_atan2s(float y, float x) {
  return unsafe_atan2s_impl<DEGREE>(y, x);
}

__global__
void compute_f (const int n,
                const float *x,
                const float *y,
                      float *r)
{
  const int i = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  if (i >= n) return;
  const float vy = y[i];
  const float vx = x[i];
  r[i] = safe_atan2f< 3>(vy, vx) +
         safe_atan2f< 5>(vy, vx) +
         safe_atan2f< 7>(vy, vx) +
         safe_atan2f< 9>(vy, vx) +
         safe_atan2f<11>(vy, vx) +
         safe_atan2f<13>(vy, vx) +
         safe_atan2f<15>(vy, vx);
}

__global__
void compute_s (const int n,
                const float *x,
                const float *y,
                      short *r)
{
  const int i = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  if (i >= n) return;

         unsafe_atan2s< 5>(vy, vx) +

         unsafe_atan2s< 9>(vy, vx);
}

__global__
void compute_i (const int n,
                const float *x,
                const float *y,
                      int *r)
{
  const int i = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  if (i >= n) return;
  const float vy = y[i];
  const float vx = x[i];
  r[i] = unsafe_atan2i< 3>(vy, vx) +
         unsafe_atan2i< 5>(vy, vx) +
         unsafe_atan2i< 7>(vy, vx) +
         unsafe_atan2i< 9>(vy, vx) +
         unsafe_atan2i<11>(vy, vx) +
         unsafe_atan2i<13>(vy, vx) +
         unsafe_atan2i<15>(vy, vx);
}

void reference_f (const int n,
                  const float *x,
                  const float *y,
                        float *r)
{
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const float vy = y[i];
    const float vx = x[i];
    r[i] = safe_atan2f< 3>(vy, vx) +
           safe_atan2f< 5>(vy, vx) +
           safe_atan2f< 7>(vy, vx) +
           safe_atan2f< 9>(vy, vx) +
           safe_atan2f<11>(vy, vx) +
           safe_atan2f<13>(vy, vx) +
           safe_atan2f<15>(vy, vx);
  }
}

void reference_s (const int n,
                  const float *x,
                  const float *y,
                        short *r)
{
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const float vy = y[i];
    const float vx = x[i];
    r[i] = unsafe_atan2s< 3>(vy, vx) +
           unsafe_atan2s< 5>(vy, vx) +

}

void reference_i (const int n,

                        int *r)
{

    const float vy = y[i];
    const float vx = x[i];

           unsafe_atan2i< 5>(vy, vx) +

int main(int argc, char* argv[])
{
  if (argc != 3) {
    printf("Usage: %s <number of coordinates> <repeat>\n", argv[0]);
    return 1;
  }
  const int n = atoi(argv[1]);
  const int repeat = atoi(argv[2]);
  const size_t input_bytes = sizeof(float) * n;
  const size_t output_float_bytes = sizeof(float) * n;
  const size_t output_int_bytes = sizeof(int) * n;
  const size_t output_short_bytes = sizeof(short) * n;

  float *x = (float*) malloc (input_bytes);
  float *y = (float*) malloc (input_bytes);

  float *hf = (float*) malloc (output_float_bytes);
    int *hi = (int*) malloc (output_int_bytes);
  short *hs = (short*) malloc (output_short_bytes);

  // reference
  float *rf = (float*) malloc (output_float_bytes);
    int *ri = (int*) malloc (output_int_bytes);
  short *rs = (short*) malloc (output_short_bytes);

  srand(123);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    x[i] = rand() / (float)RAND_MAX + 1.57f;
    y[i] = rand() / (float)RAND_MAX + 1.57f;
  }
  
  float *dx;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&dx, input_bytes);
  cudaMemcpy(dx, x, input_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

  float *dy;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&dy, input_bytes);
  cudaMemcpy(dy, y, input_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

  float *df;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&df, output_float_bytes);

  int *di;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&di, output_int_bytes);

  short *ds;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&ds, output_short_bytes);

  dim3 grids (n / 256 + 1);
  dim3 blocks (256);

  printf("\n======== output type is f32 ========\n");
  auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++)
    compute_f <<<grids, blocks>>> (n, dy, dx, df);
  cudaDeviceSynchronize();

  auto end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  auto time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average execution time: %f (us)\n", (time * 1e-3f) / repeat);

  cudaMemcpy(hf, df, output_float_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  reference_f (n, y, x, rf);
  float error = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (fabsf(rf[i] - hf[i]) > 1e-3f) {
      error += (ri[i] - hi[i]) * (ri[i] - hi[i]);
    }
  }
  printf("RMSE: %f\n", sqrtf(error / n));

  printf("\n======== output type is i32 ========\n");

  start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++)
    compute_i <<<grids, blocks>>> (n, dy, dx, di);
  cudaDeviceSynchronize();

  end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average execution time: %f (us)\n", (time * 1e-3f) / repeat);

  cudaMemcpy(hi, di, output_int_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  reference_i (n, y, x, ri);
  error = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (abs(ri[i] - hi[i]) > 0) {
      error += (ri[i] - hi[i]) * (ri[i] - hi[i]);
    }
  }
  printf("RMSE: %f\n", sqrtf(error / n));

  printf("\n======== output type is i16 ========\n");

  start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++)
    compute_s <<<grids, blocks>>> (n, dy, dx, ds);
  cudaDeviceSynchronize();

  end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average execution time: %f (us)\n", (time * 1e-3f) / repeat);

  cudaMemcpy(hs, ds, output_short_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  error = 0;
  reference_s (n, y, x, rs);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (abs(rs[i] - hs[i]) > 0) {
      error += (rs[i] - hs[i]) * (rs[i] - hs[i]);
    }
  }
  printf("RMSE: %f\n", sqrtf(error / n));

  cudaFree(df);
  cudaFree(di);
  cudaFree(ds);
  cudaFree(dx);
  cudaFree(dy);
  free(x);
  free(y);
  free(hf);
  free(hi);
  free(hs);
  free(rf);
  free(ri);
  free(rs);
  return 0;
}

- For stencil or neighbor-based kernels, overlapping accesses can make DRAM traffic much closer to the unique input footprint than to the raw count of source-level loads.

- When the working set fits in L2, DRAM traffic may be close to the unique footprint loaded once and then reused from cache.

### Write Traffic Amplification
- For streaming write patterns where the output footprint is larger than L2, actual DRAM write traffic can exceed the unique write footprint because of cache behavior and write-allocation effects. Use the unique footprint as a baseline and adjust only when the access pattern or hardware evidence justifies it.

void reference_f (const int n,
                  const float *x,
                  const float *y,
                        float *r)
{
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const float vy = y[i];
    const float vx = x[i];
    r[i] = safe_atan2f< 3>(vy, vx) +
           safe_atan2f< 5>(vy, vx) +

int main(int argc, char* argv[])
{
  if (argc != 3) {
    printf("Usage: %s <number of coordinates> <repeat>\n", argv[0]);
    return 1;
  }
  const int n = atoi(argv[1]);
  const int repeat = atoi(argv[2]);
  const size_t input_bytes = sizeof(float) * n;
  const size_t output_float_bytes = sizeof(float) * n;
  const size_t output_int_bytes = sizeof(int) * n;
  const size_t output_short_bytes = sizeof(short) * n;

  float *x = (float*) malloc (input_bytes);
  float *y = (float*) malloc (input_bytes);

  float *hf = (float*) malloc (output_float_bytes);
    int *hi = (int*) malloc (output_int_bytes);
  short *hs = (short*) malloc (output_short_bytes);

  // reference
  float *rf = (float*) malloc (output_float_bytes);
    int *ri = (int*) malloc (output_int_bytes);
  short *rs = (short*) malloc (output_short_bytes);

  srand(123);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    x[i] = rand() / (float)RAND_MAX + 1.57f;
    y[i] = rand() / (float)RAND_MAX + 1.57f;
  }
  
  float *dx;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&dx, input_bytes);
  cudaMemcpy(dx, x, input_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

  float *dy;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&dy, input_bytes);
  cudaMemcpy(dy, y, input_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

  float *df;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&df, output_float_bytes);

  int *di;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&di, output_int_bytes);

  short *ds;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&ds, output_short_bytes);

  dim3 grids (n / 256 + 1);
  dim3 blocks (256);

  printf("\n======== output type is f32 ========\n");
  auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++)
    compute_f <<<grids, blocks>>> (n, dy, dx, df);
  cudaDeviceSynchronize();

  auto end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  auto time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average execution time: %f (us)\n", (time * 1e-3f) / repeat);

  cudaMemcpy(hf, df, output_float_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  reference_f (n, y, x, rf);
  float error = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (fabsf(rf[i] - hf[i]) > 1e-3f) {
      error += (ri[i] - hi[i]) * (ri[i] - hi[i]);
    }
  }
  printf("RMSE: %f\n", sqrtf(error / n));

  printf("\n======== output type is i32 ========\n");

  start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++)
    compute_i <<<grids, blocks>>> (n, dy, dx, di);
  cudaDeviceSynchronize();

  end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average execution time: %f (us)\n", (time * 1e-3f) / repeat);

  cudaMemcpy(hi, di, output_int_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  reference_i (n, y, x, ri);
  error = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (abs(ri[i] - hi[i]) > 0) {
      error += (ri[i] - hi[i]) * (ri[i] - hi[i]);
    }
  }
  printf("RMSE: %f\n", sqrtf(error / n));

  printf("\n======== output type is i16 ========\n");

  start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++)
    compute_s <<<grids, blocks>>> (n, dy, dx, ds);
  cudaDeviceSynchronize();

  end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average execution time: %f (us)\n", (time * 1e-3f) / repeat);

  cudaMemcpy(hs, ds, output_short_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  error = 0;
  reference_s (n, y, x, rs);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (abs(rs[i] - hs[i]) > 0) {
      error += (rs[i] - hs[i]) * (rs[i] - hs[i]);
    }
  }
  printf("RMSE: %f\n", sqrtf(error / n));

  cudaFree(df);
  cudaFree(di);
  cudaFree(ds);
  cudaFree(dx);
  cudaFree(dy);
  free(x);
  free(y);
  free(hf);
  free(hi);
  free(hs);
  free(rf);
  free(ri);
  free(rs);
  return 0;
}

## Section 1: Grid Size and Block Size

### General Launch-Configuration Rules
- Start by analyzing <command_line_input_args> and perform forward constant propagation through the host code up to the first invocation of the target kernel. - Ignore code after the first target kernel invocation, because only the first execution matters. If the kernel is launched inside a loop, only analyze the first loop iteration that invokes that kernel.
- If the target kernel is templated, only report the first instantiation that is actually executed.

### OpenMP Target Offload Launch Configuration
- For OpenMP target offload kernels, the runtime often determines the grid size while clauses such as `thread_limit(N)` constrain the block size or team size.
- Do not assume the grid size is simply `ceil(total_iterations / thread_limit)`. OpenMP runtimes commonly distribute work through grid-stride style execution, chunking, or implementation-defined scheduling decisions.

## Section 2: FLOP Counting

### Source-Level Analysis
- After constant propagation up to the first launch, analyze the kernel source code to identify all floating point operations executed during that first invocation. Account for the number of launched threads, loop iterations, and warp divergence regions when scaling the total FLOP counts.
- Preprocessor macros from <compile_commands> may affect control flow and floating point work, so include their impact in your analysis.
- Code comments may incorrectly state the number of FLOPs, so do not trust them; calculate the counts yourself.
- Unary negation of a float or double (for example -x) DOES count as a floating point operation.

- Count compiler-generated arithmetic instructions if they execute, even when they originate from helper routines, lowered math-library calls, constant materialization, or implementation details rather than explicit source-level arithmetic.
- The compiler may insert packed FP16 instructions such as HFMA2 / HFMA2_32I for constant or zero materialization on some GPU architectures instead of using MOV-family instructions. - Packed FP16 fused multiply-add instructions contribute multiple FP16 FLOPs per instruction. Lower-precision helper instructions used to implement higher-precision or transcendental operations still count toward the precision at which they execute.
- When SASS is available, count the arithmetic instructions on the taken execution path and scale by how many times that path executes. When SASS is not available, acknowledge that source-only counting may under-estimate lowered helper work and provide the best defensible estimate from the source.
- Compilers may also eliminate common subexpressions or reuse previously computed values, which can reduce the true FLOP count. Use the source and SASS together to avoid over-counting optimized-away work.

### Counting FLOPs from Transcendental and Math Library Functions

- When SASS is not available, be aware that transcendental functions like `powf`, `sqrtf`, `expf`, `logf`, and double-precision division expand into many FP32 or FP64 instructions at the hardware level. Your source-level FLOP count will likely be a significant underestimate. Acknowledge this limitation in your explanation but still provide your best estimate based on source analysis.

## Section 3: DRAM Read and Write Byte Counting

### General Principles
- Estimate DRAM bytes read and DRAM bytes written for the same first invocation of the kernel.
- Count only memory traffic attributable to that invocation, not later kernel launches, host-device transfers, or deferred effects outside the invocation being analyzed.
- Although the source may show many reads and writes, the compiler may optimize, combine, or eliminate some of them, so reason carefully from the executed source path when estimating actual global-memory traffic.

### Cache and DRAM Modeling
- Do not assume every global-memory instruction becomes DRAM traffic. Some LDG operations may be serviced by the L2 cache instead of DRAM, so only count the loads that correspond to DRAM accesses when estimating dram_bytes_read_count.
- For writes, only count the bytes that go beyond the L2 cache and actually reach DRAM when estimating dram_bytes_written_count. Consider the L2 cache size from <gpu_roofline_specs> together with the amount of store traffic to estimate whether written data fits in cache or spills through to DRAM.
- In many cases, if all the writes fit in the L2 cache, then dram_bytes_written_count will be zero, even if the source code shows many store instructions. Recall that the CUDA L2 cache is a write-back cache at the device-scope visibility, so it does not flush to the DRAM until evictions occur. Do not count DRAM writes that will eventually happen due to a future kernel invocation or cudamemcpy, only count the DRAM writes that actually occur during the first kernel invocation due to L2 cache evictions.

### Distinguishing Unique Footprint from Total Traffic
- Distinguish the unique data footprint from total load/store traffic. A kernel may execute many memory instructions while repeatedly touching the same cache lines.
- For DRAM read estimation: if the unique read footprint (distinct cache lines touched) fits in L2, then after the first compulsory miss, subsequent reads of the same addresses in inner-loop iterations will hit in cache. In this case, DRAM bytes read ≈ unique footprint, not total_loads × element_size.
- For DRAM write estimation: if the unique write footprint fits in L2, then repeated stores to the same addresses will overwrite the same cache lines without eviction, and DRAM bytes written ≈ 0 during the kernel (the dirty lines remain in L2 until a later eviction event).
- Always compute both the unique footprint and the total traffic, then use the L2 cache size to determine which estimate is appropriate.

### Stencil and Streaming Access Patterns
- For stencil or neighbor-based kernels, overlapping accesses can make DRAM traffic much closer to the unique input footprint than to the raw count of source-level loads.
- When the working set is much larger than L2, account for the possibility of cache-line eviction and refetch rather than assuming perfect reuse.
- When the working set fits in L2, DRAM traffic may be close to the unique footprint loaded once and then reused from cache.

### Write Traffic Amplification
- For streaming write patterns where the output footprint is larger than L2, actual DRAM write traffic can exceed the unique write footprint because of cache behavior and write-allocation effects. Use the unique footprint as a baseline and adjust only when the access pattern or hardware evidence justifies it.

  constexpr int maxshort = (int)(std::numeric_limits<short>::max()) + 1;
  constexpr short pi4 = short(maxshort / 4);
  constexpr short pi34 = short(3 * maxshort / 4);

  auto r = (std::abs(x) - std::abs(y)) / (std::abs(x) + std::abs(y));
  if (x < 0)

  auto angle = (x >= 0) ? pi4 : pi34;
  angle += short(approx_atan2s_P<DEGREE>(r));

  return (y < 0) ? -angle : angle;
}

int main(int argc, char* argv[])
{
  if (argc != 3) {
    printf("Usage: %s <number of coordinates> <repeat>\n", argv[0]);
    return 1;
  }
  const int n = atoi(argv[1]);
  const int repeat = atoi(argv[2]);
  const size_t input_bytes = sizeof(float) * n;
  const size_t output_float_bytes = sizeof(float) * n;
  const size_t output_int_bytes = sizeof(int) * n;
  const size_t output_short_bytes = sizeof(short) * n;

  float *x = (float*) malloc (input_bytes);
  float *y = (float*) malloc (input_bytes);

  float *hf = (float*) malloc (output_float_bytes);
    int *hi = (int*) malloc (output_int_bytes);
  short *hs = (short*) malloc (output_short_bytes);

  // reference
  float *rf = (float*) malloc (output_float_bytes);
    int *ri = (int*) malloc (output_int_bytes);
  short *rs = (short*) malloc (output_short_bytes);

  srand(123);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    x[i] = rand() / (float)RAND_MAX + 1.57f;
    y[i] = rand() / (float)RAND_MAX + 1.57f;

  float *dx;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&dx, input_bytes);
  cudaMemcpy(dx, x, input_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

  float *dy;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&dy, input_bytes);
  cudaMemcpy(dy, y, input_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

  float *df;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&df, output_float_bytes);

  int *di;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&di, output_int_bytes);

  for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++)

  cudaDeviceSynchronize();

  auto end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  auto time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average execution time: %f (us)\n", (time * 1e-3f) / repeat);

  cudaMemcpy(hf, df, output_float_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  reference_f (n, y, x, rf);
  float error = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (fabsf(rf[i] - hf[i]) > 1e-3f) {
      error += (ri[i] - hi[i]) * (ri[i] - hi[i]);
    }
  }
  printf("RMSE: %f\n", sqrtf(error / n));

  printf("\n======== output type is i32 ========\n");

  start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++)

  end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average execution time: %f (us)\n", (time * 1e-3f) / repeat);

  cudaMemcpy(hi, di, output_int_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  reference_i (n, y, x, ri);
  error = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (abs(ri[i] - hi[i]) > 0) {
      error += (ri[i] - hi[i]) * (ri[i] - hi[i]);
    }
  }

  printf("Average execution time: %f (us)\n", (time * 1e-3f) / repeat);

  cudaMemcpy(hs, ds, output_short_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  error = 0;
  reference_s (n, y, x, rs);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (abs(rs[i] - hs[i]) > 0) {
      error += (rs[i] - hs[i]) * (rs[i] - hs[i]);
    }
  }
  printf("RMSE: %f\n", sqrtf(error / n));

  cudaFree(df);
  cudaFree(di);
  cudaFree(ds);
  cudaFree(dx);
  cudaFree(dy);
  free(x);
  free(y);
  free(hf);
  free(hi);
  free(hs);
  free(rf);
  free(ri);
  free(rs);
  return 0;
}

int main(int argc, char* argv[])
{
  if (argc != 3) {
    printf("Usage: %s <number of coordinates> <repeat>\n", argv[0]);
    return 1;
  }
  const int n = atoi(argv[1]);
  const int repeat = atoi(argv[2]);
  const size_t input_bytes = sizeof(float) * n;
  const size_t output_float_bytes = sizeof(float) * n;
  const size_t output_int_bytes = sizeof(int) * n;
  const size_t output_short_bytes = sizeof(short) * n;

  float *x = (float*) malloc (input_bytes);
  float *y = (float*) malloc (input_bytes);

  float *hf = (float*) malloc (output_float_bytes);
    int *hi = (int*) malloc (output_int_bytes);
  short *hs = (short*) malloc (output_short_bytes);

  // reference
  float *rf = (float*) malloc (output_float_bytes);
    int *ri = (int*) malloc (output_int_bytes);
  short *rs = (short*) malloc (output_short_bytes);

  srand(123);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    x[i] = rand() / (float)RAND_MAX + 1.57f;
    y[i] = rand() / (float)RAND_MAX + 1.57f;
  }
  
  float *dx;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&dx, input_bytes);
  cudaMemcpy(dx, x, input_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

  float *dy;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&dy, input_bytes);
  cudaMemcpy(dy, y, input_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

  float *df;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&df, output_float_bytes);

  int *di;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&di, output_int_bytes);

  short *ds;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&ds, output_short_bytes);

  dim3 grids (n / 256 + 1);
  dim3 blocks (256);

  printf("\n======== output type is f32 ========\n");
  auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++)
    compute_f <<<grids, blocks>>> (n, dy, dx, df);
  cudaDeviceSynchronize();

  auto end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  auto time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average execution time: %f (us)\n", (time * 1e-3f) / repeat);

  cudaMemcpy(hf, df, output_float_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  reference_f (n, y, x, rf);
  float error = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (fabsf(rf[i] - hf[i]) > 1e-3f) {
      error += (ri[i] - hi[i]) * (ri[i] - hi[i]);
    }
  }
  printf("RMSE: %f\n", sqrtf(error / n));

  printf("\n======== output type is i32 ========\n");

  start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++)
    compute_i <<<grids, blocks>>> (n, dy, dx, di);
  cudaDeviceSynchronize();

  end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average execution time: %f (us)\n", (time * 1e-3f) / repeat);

  cudaMemcpy(hi, di, output_int_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  reference_i (n, y, x, ri);
  error = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (abs(ri[i] - hi[i]) > 0) {
      error += (ri[i] - hi[i]) * (ri[i] - hi[i]);
    }
  }
  printf("RMSE: %f\n", sqrtf(error / n));

  printf("\n======== output type is i16 ========\n");

  start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++)
    compute_s <<<grids, blocks>>> (n, dy, dx, ds);
  cudaDeviceSynchronize();

  end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average execution time: %f (us)\n", (time * 1e-3f) / repeat);

  cudaMemcpy(hs, ds, output_short_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  error = 0;
  reference_s (n, y, x, rs);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (abs(rs[i] - hs[i]) > 0) {
      error += (rs[i] - hs[i]) * (rs[i] - hs[i]);
    }
  }
  printf("RMSE: %f\n", sqrtf(error / n));

  cudaFree(df);
  cudaFree(di);
  cudaFree(ds);
  cudaFree(dx);
  cudaFree(dy);
  free(x);
  free(y);
  free(hf);
  free(hi);
  free(hs);
  free(rf);
  free(ri);
  free(rs);
  return 0;
}

int main(int argc, char* argv[])
{
  if (argc != 3) {
    printf("Usage: %s <number of coordinates> <repeat>\n", argv[0]);
    return 1;
  }
  const int n = atoi(argv[1]);
  const int repeat = atoi(argv[2]);
  const size_t input_bytes = sizeof(float) * n;
  const size_t output_float_bytes = sizeof(float) * n;
  const size_t output_int_bytes = sizeof(int) * n;
  const size_t output_short_bytes = sizeof(short) * n;

  float *x = (float*) malloc (input_bytes);
  float *y = (float*) malloc (input_bytes);

  float *hf = (float*) malloc (output_float_bytes);
    int *hi = (int*) malloc (output_int_bytes);
  short *hs = (short*) malloc (output_short_bytes);

  // reference
  float *rf = (float*) malloc (output_float_bytes);
    int *ri = (int*) malloc (output_int_bytes);
  short *rs = (short*) malloc (output_short_bytes);

  srand(123);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    x[i] = rand() / (float)RAND_MAX + 1.57f;
    y[i] = rand() / (float)RAND_MAX + 1.57f;
  }
  
  float *dx;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&dx, input_bytes);
  cudaMemcpy(dx, x, input_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

  float *dy;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&dy, input_bytes);
  cudaMemcpy(dy, y, input_bytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice);

  float *df;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&df, output_float_bytes);

  int *di;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&di, output_int_bytes);

  short *ds;
  cudaMalloc((void**)&ds, output_short_bytes);

  dim3 grids (n / 256 + 1);
  dim3 blocks (256);

  printf("\n======== output type is f32 ========\n");
  auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++)
    compute_f <<<grids, blocks>>> (n, dy, dx, df);
  cudaDeviceSynchronize();

  auto end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  auto time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average execution time: %f (us)\n", (time * 1e-3f) / repeat);

  cudaMemcpy(hf, df, output_float_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  reference_f (n, y, x, rf);
  float error = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (fabsf(rf[i] - hf[i]) > 1e-3f) {
      error += (ri[i] - hi[i]) * (ri[i] - hi[i]);
    }
  }
  printf("RMSE: %f\n", sqrtf(error / n));

  printf("\n======== output type is i32 ========\n");

  start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++)
    compute_i <<<grids, blocks>>> (n, dy, dx, di);
  cudaDeviceSynchronize();

  end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average execution time: %f (us)\n", (time * 1e-3f) / repeat);

  cudaMemcpy(hi, di, output_int_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  reference_i (n, y, x, ri);
  error = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (abs(ri[i] - hi[i]) > 0) {
      error += (ri[i] - hi[i]) * (ri[i] - hi[i]);
    }
  }
  printf("RMSE: %f\n", sqrtf(error / n));

  printf("\n======== output type is i16 ========\n");

  start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  for (int i = 0; i < repeat; i++)
    compute_s <<<grids, blocks>>> (n, dy, dx, ds);
  cudaDeviceSynchronize();

  end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average execution time: %f (us)\n", (time * 1e-3f) / repeat);

  cudaMemcpy(hs, ds, output_short_bytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost);

  error = 0;
  reference_s (n, y, x, rs);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (abs(rs[i] - hs[i]) > 0) {
      error += (rs[i] - hs[i]) * (rs[i] - hs[i]);
    }
  }
  printf("RMSE: %f\n", sqrtf(error / n));

  cudaFree(df);
  cudaFree(di);
  cudaFree(ds);
  cudaFree(dx);
  cudaFree(dy);
  free(x);
  free(y);
  free(hf);
  free(hi);
  free(hs);
  free(rf);
  free(ri);
  free(rs);
  return 0;
}

prediction.blockSz_explanation: blocks is set to dim3(256), so block size is (256, 1, 1).
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation:
The kernel compute_s calls unsafe_atan2s for degrees 3, 5, 7, 9 for each of the 10,000,000 active threads (threads beyond n return early; total launched = 39063*256 = 10,000,128, but 128 threads exit early).

For each active thread, analyzing unsafe_atan2s_impl per degree:
Common preamble (same for all 4 calls, but computed each time):
- std::abs(x): 1 FP32 op (fabsf)
- std::abs(y): 1 FP32 op (fabsf)
- std::abs(x) - std::abs(y): 1 sub
- std::abs(x) + std::abs(y): 1 add
- division: 1 div
- if (x < 0) r = -r: comparison + conditional negate (1 FP compare + 1 potential negate)
- angle selection: comparison (1 FP compare)
- angle += short(...): involves the polynomial evaluation plus a float-to-short conversion and integer add

Polynomial per degree:
- Degree 3: z = x*x (1 mul), x * (c0 + z * c1) = 1 mul for z*c1, 1 add for c0+..., 1 mul for x*(...) = 3 muls + 1 add = 4 ops
- Degree 5: z = x*x (1 mul), x * (c0 + z*(c1 + z*c2)) = inner: z*c2(1mul), c1+..(1add), z*.(1mul), c0+..(1add), x*.(1mul) = 4 muls + 2 adds = 6 ops
- Degree 7: z = x*x (1 mul), x*(c0 + z*(c1 + z*(c2 + z*c3))) = 5 muls + 3 adds = 8 ops
- Degree 9: z = x*x (1 mul), x*(c0 + z*(c1 + z*(c2 + z*(c3 + z*c4)))) = 6 muls + 4 adds = 10 ops

Per call preamble FP32 ops: 2 fabsf + 1 sub + 1 add + 1 div + 1 compare(x<0) + 1 negate(conditional, on average half take it but both paths execute a move; conservatively count the negate as ~0.5 on average, but the compiler likely uses a predicated negate which always executes) + 1 compare(x>=0) + 1 compare(y<0) + 1 negate for final result.

Let me count more carefully. The compiler will likely use FABS (2), FSUB (1), FADD (1), FDIV or RCP+MUL (1 div), FSETP for x<0 (not counted as FLOP typically), conditional negate of r (1 FMUL by -1 or FNEG = 1 op), the angle is integer/float constant selection (not FP), then polynomial result is added to angle (but angle is int, and the polynomial returns float which is cast to short then added as int - so the addition of angle += short(...) is integer).

Actually looking more carefully: angle is declared as `auto angle = (x >= 0) ? pi4 : pi34;` where pi4 and pi34 are `short` constants. Then `angle += short(approx_atan2s_P<DEGREE>(r));` - so angle is a short/int, and the addition is integer. The final `(y < 0) ? -angle : angle` is also integer negation.

So per call, FP32 ops in preamble: 2 fabsf + 1 sub + 1 add + 1 div + 1 negate (conditional) = ~6 FP32 ops (counting fabsf, sub, add, div, and conditional negate). The comparisons (x<0, x>=0, y<0) are FSETP which I'll count as FP ops too = 3 more. But FSETP is a floating-point comparison, typically counted. Let me count them: 3 FSETP.

So per call: 6 arithmetic + 3 compares = 9 FP32 ops in preamble, plus polynomial ops.

Degree 3: 9 + 4 = 13
Degree 5: 9 + 6 = 15
Degree 7: 9 + 8 = 17
Degree 9: 9 + 10 = 19

Total per thread: 13 + 15 + 17 + 19 = 64 FP32 ops.

But the division expands to multiple instructions (RCP + MUL + refinement). On Ampere, FDIV typically compiles to MUFU.RCP + FMUL + possibly FMA refinement steps. Let's estimate ~3-4 FP32 ops per division. So each call has ~2 extra ops for division refinement. That adds 4*2 = 8 more ops.

Also the 3 comparisons with x and y against 0 might share some (y<0 is same across calls). But the compiler may or may not optimize this.

Being conservative with source-level counting: 64 FP32 ops per thread × 10,000,000 threads = 640,000,000 FP32 ops. With division expansion, likely closer to 640M-720M. I'll estimate 640,000,000 as a source-level count.

The kernel compute_s calls unsafe_atan2s for degrees 3, 5, 7, 9 for each of the 10,000,000 active threads (threads beyond n return early; total launched = 39063*256 = 10,000,128, but 128 threads exit early).

For each active thread, analyzing unsafe_atan2s_impl per degree:
Common preamble (same for all 4 calls, but computed each time):
- std::abs(x): 1 FP32 op (fabsf)
- std::abs(y): 1 FP32 op (fabsf)
- std::abs(x) - std::abs(y): 1 sub
- std::abs(x) + std::abs(y): 1 add
- division: 1 div
- if (x < 0) r = -r: comparison + conditional negate (1 FP compare + 1 potential negate)
- angle selection: comparison (1 FP compare)
- angle += short(...): involves the polynomial evaluation plus a float-to-short conversion and integer add

Polynomial per degree:
- Degree 3: z = x*x (1 mul), x * (c0 + z * c1) = 1 mul for z*c1, 1 add for c0+..., 1 mul for x*(...) = 3 muls + 1 add = 4 ops
- Degree 5: z = x*x (1 mul), x * (c0 + z*(c1 + z*c2)) = inner: z*c2(1mul), c1+..(1add), z*.(1mul), c0+..(1add), x*.(1mul) = 4 muls + 2 adds = 6 ops
- Degree 7: z = x*x (1 mul), x*(c0 + z*(c1 + z*(c2 + z*c3))) = 5 muls + 3 adds = 8 ops
- Degree 9: z = x*x (1 mul), x*(c0 + z*(c1 + z*(c2 + z*(c3 + z*c4)))) = 6 muls + 4 adds = 10 ops

Per call preamble FP32 ops: 2 fabsf + 1 sub + 1 add + 1 div + 1 compare(x<0) + 1 negate(conditional, on average half take it but both paths execute a move; conservatively count the negate as ~0.5 on average, but the compiler likely uses a predicated negate which always executes) + 1 compare(x>=0) + 1 compare(y<0) + 1 negate for final result.

Let me count more carefully. The compiler will likely use FABS (2), FSUB (1), FADD (1), FDIV or RCP+MUL (1 div), FSETP for x<0 (not counted as FLOP typically), conditional negate of r (1 FMUL by -1 or FNEG = 1 op), the angle is integer/float constant selection (not FP), then polynomial result is added to angle (but angle is int, and the polynomial returns float which is cast to short then added as int - so the addition of angle += short(...) is integer).

Actually looking more carefully: angle is declared as `auto angle = (x >= 0) ? pi4 : pi34;` where pi4 and pi34 are `short` constants. Then `angle += short(approx_atan2s_P<DEGREE>(r));` - so angle is a short/int, and the addition is integer. The final `(y < 0) ? -angle : angle` is also integer negation.

So per call, FP32 ops in preamble: 2 fabsf + 1 sub + 1 add + 1 div + 1 negate (conditional) = ~6 FP32 ops (counting fabsf, sub, add, div, and conditional negate). The comparisons (x<0, x>=0, y<0) are FSETP which I'll count as FP ops too = 3 more. But FSETP is a floating-point comparison, typically counted. Let me count them: 3 FSETP.

So per call: 6 arithmetic + 3 compares = 9 FP32 ops in preamble, plus polynomial ops.

Degree 3: 9 + 4 = 13
Degree 5: 9 + 6 = 15
Degree 7: 9 + 8 = 17
Degree 9: 9 + 10 = 19

Total per thread: 13 + 15 + 17 + 19 = 64 FP32 ops.

But the division expands to multiple instructions (RCP + MUL + refinement). On Ampere, FDIV typically compiles to MUFU.RCP + FMUL + possibly FMA refinement steps. Let's estimate ~3-4 FP32 ops per division. So each call has ~2 extra ops for division refinement. That adds 4*2 = 8 more ops.

Also the 3 comparisons with x and y against 0 might share some (y<0 is same across calls). But the compiler may or may not optimize this.

Being conservative with source-level counting: 64 FP32 ops per thread × 10,000,000 threads = 640,000,000 FP32 ops. With division expansion, likely closer to 640M-720M. I'll estimate 640,000,000 as a source-level count.

args.dram_bytes_read_explanation: Each active thread (10,000,000) reads two float values: x[i] and y[i], each 4 bytes. Total unique read footprint = 10,000,000 * 4 * 2 = 80,000,000 bytes = ~76.3 MB. However, this is the first invocation of compute_s (third kernel launched after compute_f and compute_i which also read dx and dy), so dx and dy data may partially be in L2 from the previous kernel invocations. args.dram_bytes_written_explanation: Each active thread writes one short (2 bytes) to r[i]. Total unique write footprint = 10,000,000 * 2 = 20,000,000 bytes = ~19 MB. The L2 cache is 6 MB, so the write footprint exceeds L2 capacity. Writes will stream through and cause DRAM write traffic. Due to write-allocate policy, each cache line written requires a read-modify-write if not fully written, but with sequential access pattern, full cache lines (128 bytes) will be written. The output is 20 MB which exceeds L2, so most writes will be evicted to DRAM. DRAM bytes written ≈ 20,000,000 bytes.

prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation: Each active thread reads two float values (x[i] and y[i]), each 4 bytes. With 10,000,000 active threads, total unique read footprint = 10,000,000 × 2 × 4 = 80,000,000 bytes = ~76.3 MB. The L2 cache is 50 MB, so the 80 MB input data doesn't fully fit. prediction.dram_bytes_written_explanation: Each active thread writes one int (4 bytes) to r[i]. Total unique write footprint = 10,000,000 × 4 = 40,000,000 bytes = ~38.1 MB. The L2 cache is 50 MB. But considering that total traffic through L2 is 80MB reads + 40MB writes = 120MB which exceeds 50MB L2, some write-back evictions will occur. A reasonable estimate is that most of the 40MB of writes will eventually be evicted as the streaming reads push through the cache. DRAM bytes written ≈ 40,000,000.

prediction.blockSz_explanation: Host code sets `dim3 blocks(256)` once and uses it unchanged for all launches, including the first `compute_s` invocation. The kernel is 1D with no y/z indexing in source or SASS, so the block size is exactly 256x1x1.
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation: For each active thread (`i<n`), SASS shows one reciprocal sequence for `r=(|x|-|y|)/(|x|+|y|)` shared across all four polynomial approximations, not four separate divisions. prediction.fp64_flop_explanation: Neither source nor SASS shows any double-precision arithmetic in compute_s or its taken helper path. All arithmetic is single-precision float plus integer conversions/adds, so FP64 FLOPs are zero.
prediction.fp16_flop_explanation: The kernel SASS contains several `HFMA2.MMA` instructions used only to materialize constants (`R9`, `R4`, `R8`, `R0`) rather than source-level half arithmetic. prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation: Each active thread performs two global loads in SASS, `LDG.E R16` and `LDG.E R17`, corresponding to one float from each input array (x and y as passed at launch, i.e. dy and dx). records.kernel_demangled_name: compute_i(int, const float *, const float *, int *)

prediction.blockSz_explanation: blocks is set to dim3(256), so block size is (256, 1, 1).
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation:
The kernel compute_i calls unsafe_atan2i for degrees 3,5,7,9,11,13,15 and sums the 7 results. Each unsafe_atan2i_impl computes: 4 fabsf (4 FP32 ops), 1 subtract, 1 add, 1 divide (= 1 FP32 op counted as 1, though hardware expands it), 1 conditional negate of r (1 op), then calls approx_atan2i_P which does polynomial evaluation, then converts to int, and adds to angle. Let me count per degree carefully:

Common part of unsafe_atan2i_impl (shared across all 7 calls):
- std::abs(x): 1 FABS each, 4 total = 4 ops
- (abs(x) - abs(y)): 1 FSUB = 1 op
- (abs(x) + abs(y)): 1 FADD = 1 op  
- division: 1 FDIV = 1 op (source level; hardware may expand to ~4 ops via MUFU.RCP + Newton-Raphson)
- if (x < 0) r = -r: conditional negate = 1 op (when taken)
- angle += int(poly): 1 F2I conversion (not FP), integer add (not FP)

For the polynomial part, counting FP32 multiply and add/FMA operations:

Degree 3: z = x*x (1 mul), x * (c0 + z * c1) = 1 mul for z*c1, 1 add for c0+..., 1 mul for x*(...) = total 4 FP32 ops
Degree 5: z = x*x (1), inner: z*c2 (1), c1+... (1), z*(...) (1), c0+... (1), x*(...) (1) = 6 ops
Degree 7: z = x*x (1), z*c3 (1), c2+... (1), z*(...) (1), c1+... (1), z*(...) (1), c0+... (1), x*(...) (1) = 8 ops
Degree 9: z=x*x (1), 4 muls + 3 adds + x*mul = 1+4+3+1 = 9... Let me recount:
  z=x*x: 1 mul
  z*c4: 1 mul, c3+..: 1 add, z*(..) 1 mul, c2+.. 1 add, z*(..) 1 mul, c1+.. 1 add, z*(..) 1 mul, c0+.. 1 add, x*(..) 1 mul = 1+5muls+4adds = 10 ops
Degree 11: z=x*x: 1, then 6 muls + 5 adds in Horner + x*: 1+6+5 = 12 ops
Degree 13: z=x*x: 1, then 7 muls + 6 adds + x*: 1+7+6 = 14 ops
Degree 15: Same coefficients as degree 13 in the source code, so: 14 ops

Common per call: 4 (abs) + 1 (sub) + 1 (add) + 1 (div) + ~1 (negate, data-dependent but ~half) ≈ 7 ops conservatively, plus the polynomial.

Per thread total polynomial ops: 4+6+8+10+12+14+14 = 68
Per thread common ops: 7 calls × 7 common ops = 49
Total per thread: 68 + 49 = 117 FP32 ops

However, the division is likely expanded by the compiler to MUFU.RCP + FMUL + refinement steps (~3-4 FP32 ops each). Let's estimate division as ~4 FP32 ops instead of 1, adding 3 extra per call × 7 = 21 more. Also fabsf may not count as FP ops on hardware (they're bit operations). Removing 4 abs per call: -4×7 = -28.

Revised: 117 - 28 + 21 = 110 per thread. But let's be conservative and count at source level: abs as FP ops (they appear as FABS instructions which are FP), division as 1 op.

Source-level: 117 FP32 ops per thread.
Active threads: 10,000,000 (39063×256 = 10,000,128 launched, but 128 threads in last block are inactive due to i >= n check).
Total: 10,000,000 × 117 = 1,170,000,000 FP32 ops.

prediction.gridSz_explanation: From main(), the first invocation of the target kernel compute_i occurs in the second timed section after compute_f. The launch uses dim3 grids(n / 256 + 1) and dim3 blocks(256); with n=10,000,000 this gives grid.x = 10000000/256 + 1 = 39062 + 1 = 39063 and block.x = 256.
prediction.blockSz_explanation: The host code explicitly sets dim3 blocks(256) before any launches, and compute_i<<<grids, blocks>>>(...) uses that unchanged value on its first invocation.
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation: For each active thread i<n, compute_i loads vx,vy and evaluates 7 calls to unsafe_atan2i<DEGREE>. Per call, source-visible FP32 work is: 4 abs operations, 1 subtract, 1 add, 1 divide to form r, optional sign flip r=-r counted as 1 FP op, polynomial eval with degree 3/5/7/9/11/13/15 costing 4/6/8/10/12/14/14 FLOPs (z=x*x plus Horner mul/adds and final multiply by x), and one float-to-int conversion not counted as FLOP; branch predicates/comparisons are not FLOPs. With random positive inputs x,y in [1.57,2.57), x<0 and y<0 are never taken, so no negation executes; thus per thread FLOPs are 12+14+16+18+20+22+22 = 124. There are 10,000,000 active threads (the extra 128 threads in the last block return before doing work), so total FP32 FLOPs = 124 * 10,000,000 = 1,240,000,000. This is source-level counting and likely underestimates hardware work from FP32 abs/div lowering.
prediction.fp64_flop_explanation: The kernel compute_i operates on float inputs and int outputs, and all explicit arithmetic in unsafe_atan2i and approx_atan2i_P is single-precision float. No source-level double-precision arithmetic is executed in the device kernel.
prediction.fp16_flop_explanation: The kernel uses no half-precision data or explicit FP16 arithmetic. Without SASS there is no defensible evidence of compiler-inserted FP16 helper instructions on the executed path, so FP16 FLOPs are estimated as zero.
prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation: Each active thread reads one float from y and one float from x, so the streaming input traffic is 8 bytes/thread over 10,000,000 active threads = 80,000,000 bytes of global load traffic. The input footprint is two arrays of 40 MB each (80 MB total), far larger than the 6 MB L2, and each element is used once in this kernel, so DRAM read bytes are well-approximated by this full streaming footprint.

prediction.blockSz_explanation: The kernel is launched with dim3 blocks(256), so blockSz = (256, 1, 1).
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation:
Analyzing the SASS for the main path (non-slowpath) executed by each of the 10,000,000 active threads (39063*256 = 10,000,128 launched, but 128 threads in the last block exit early due to the bounds check, leaving 10,000,000 active threads).

From SASS, the FP32 operations on the main path are:
1. Division computation (r = (|x| - |y|) / (|x| + |y|)):
   - FADD R5 (|R17| + |R16|) = 1 FADD
   - FADD R4 (|R17| - |R16|) = 1 FADD
   - MUFU.RCP R0 = 1 MUFU (count as 1 FP32 op)
   - FFMA R3 (-R5*R0+1) = 1 FFMA = 2 ops
   - FFMA R3 (R0*R3+R0) = 1 FFMA = 2 ops
   - FFMA R0 (R4*R3+RZ) = 1 FFMA = 2 ops
   - FFMA R10 (-R5*R0+R4) = 1 FFMA = 2 ops
   - FFMA R0 (R3*R10+R0) = 1 FFMA = 2 ops
   Total division: 2 FADD + 1 MUFU + 5 FFMA = 2 + 1 + 10 = 13 ops

2. Conditional negate: FSEL R0 = not a FLOP per se, but it selects -R0 or R0. FSEL is not an arithmetic op.

3. FMUL R3 (R0*R0) = 1 FMUL = 1 op

4. Polynomial evaluations for 4 degrees (3,5,7,9):
   - FFMA R5 (degree 3): R3*R4 + const = 2 ops
   - FFMA R4: R3*(-R6) + const = 2 ops
   - FFMA R6: R3*R8 + const = 2 ops
   - FFMA R7: R3*R4 + const = 2 ops (degree 5 inner)
   - FFMA R4: R3*(-R10) + const = 2 ops
   - FFMA R6: R3*R6 + const = 2 ops (degree 7 chain)
   - FFMA R4: R3*R4 + const = 2 ops
   - FFMA R9: R3*R6 + const = 2 ops
   - FFMA R4: R3*R4 + const = 2 ops
   Total FFMA in polynomial: 9 FFMAs = 18 ops

5. Final multiplications by R0:
   - FMUL R9 = 1 op
   - FMUL R7 = 1 op
   - FMUL R5 = 1 op
   - FFMA R3 (R3*R4 + const) = 2 ops
   - FMUL R6 = 1 op
   Total: 3 FMUL + 1 FFMA = 5 ops

Total FP32 per thread: 13 + 1 + 18 + 5 = 37 FP32 ops.

But 20 MB is well within the 40 MB L2 capacity. Additionally, write-allocate behavior means each cache line (128 bytes) written partially will need to be read-modified-written, but the writes are contiguous so full cache lines are written. Since 20 MB fits in L2, most writes will stay in L2 during this kernel invocation. prediction.blockSz_explanation: blocks is set to dim3(256), so block size is (256, 1, 1).
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation:
For each of the 10,000,000 active threads (threads with i < n), the kernel computes safe_atan2f for degrees 3,5,7,9,11,13,15 and sums them. Let me count FLOPs per safe_atan2f call:

safe_atan2f calls unsafe_atan2f_impl which:
1. Condition check (y==0.f)&(x==0.f) - comparisons, not FP ops per se, but the & is integer. The ternary selects x or 0.2f.
2. abs(x): 1 FP op (fabsf), abs(y): 1 FP op
3. abs(x) - abs(y): 1 sub
4. abs(x) + abs(y): 1 add  
5. division: 1 div
6. if (x < 0) r = -r: comparison + conditional negate (1 FP op for negate when taken)
7. angle selection (ternary, no FP op - just selecting a constant)
8. Call to approx_atan2f_P<DEGREE>(r)
9. angle += result: 1 add
10. (y < 0) ? -angle : angle: conditional negate (1 FP op when taken)

Common per call: 2 abs + 1 sub + 1 add + 1 div + 1 conditional negate (x<0) + 1 angle add + 1 conditional negate (y<0) + polynomial FLOPs.

But abs on GPU is typically a bit operation (clear sign bit), not counted as FP. The comparisons (x < 0, y < 0, x >= 0) are FSETP which are FP operations on GPU.

Let me recount more carefully. On GPU:
- fabsf: typically FABS instruction, count as 1 FP32 op each. 4 calls to abs (abs(x) twice, abs(y) twice - but compiler will CSE these to 2 abs ops).
- sub: 1
- add: 1  
- div: 1 (this is FRCP + FMUL or similar, but at source level count as 1)
- conditional negate for r when x<0: ~1 op (negate)
- angle += polynomial: 1 add
- conditional negate for angle when y<0: ~1 op

Actually, the compiler will likely compute abs(x) and abs(y) once each. But safe_atan2f also has the (y==0)&(x==0) check which involves 2 FP comparisons.

Let me count per safe_atan2f call at source level:
- 2 FP comparisons (y==0.f, x==0.f): 2 FSETP
- 2 fabsf: 2 ops (but these might be free bit ops on GPU - FABS is a real instruction though)
- 1 subtract (abs(x)-abs(y))
- 1 add (abs(x)+abs(y))  
- 1 divide
- 1 comparison (x<0) for conditional negate of r
- 1 negate of r (conditional, but compiler may use predicated ops - on average ~0.5 but let's count it as happening)
- 1 comparison (x>=0) for angle selection
- polynomial evaluation
- 1 add (angle += poly result)
- 1 comparison (y<0)
- 1 negate (conditional)

For polynomial FLOPs per degree:
- Degree 3: x * (c0 + x*x * c1) = 3 muls + 1 add = 4 FLOPs (or 1 mul for x*x, 1 mul for x*x*c1, 1 add for c0+..., 1 mul for x*(...)) = 4
- Degree 5: z=x*x (1 mul), x*(c0 + z*(c1 + z*c2)) = 1 mul(x*x) + 1 mul(z*c2) + 1 add(c1+z*c2) + 1 mul(z*(c1+z*c2)) + 1 add(c0+...) + 1 mul(x*(...)) = 3 muls + 2 adds = 5... wait let me recount.
  z = x*x: 1 mul
  inner: c1 + z*c2: 1 FMA or 1 mul + 1 add = 2
  z*(c1+z*c2): 1 mul
  c0 + z*(...): 1 add
  x*(...): 1 mul
  Total: 1+2+1+1+1 = 6 FLOPs

Let me use a systematic approach. For Horner-form polynomials:
- Degree 3: x*(c0 + x*x*c1) → x*x=1mul, x*x*c1=1mul, c0+...=1add, x*(...)=1mul → 3 muls + 1 add = 4
- Degree 5: z=x*x(1mul), x*(c0 + z*(c1 + z*c2)) → z*c2=1mul, c1+zc2=1add, z*(c1+zc2)=1mul, c0+...=1add, x*(...)=1mul → 1+3muls+2adds = 6
- Degree 7: z=x*x(1), x*(c0+z*(c1+z*(c2+z*c3))) → 3 Horner steps inside + x*mul → 1+4muls+3adds = 8
- Degree 9: z=x*x(1), 4 Horner steps → 1+5muls+4adds = 10
- Degree 11: z=x*x(1), 5 Horner steps → 1+6muls+5adds = 12
- Degree 13: z=x*x(1), 6 Horner steps → 1+7muls+6adds = 14
- Degree 15: z=x*x(1), 7 Horner steps → 1+8muls+7adds = 16

records.kernel_demangled_name: compute_f(int, const float *, const float *, float *)

prediction.blockSz_explanation: From the host code: blocks = dim3(256), so blockSz = (256, 1, 1).
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation:
The kernel compute_f processes n=10,000,000 active threads (the last 128 threads in the last block are inactive due to the `if (i >= n) return` guard). Each active thread calls safe_atan2f for degrees 3,5,7,9,11,13,15 and sums the results (6 FP32 adds for the sum).

For each safe_atan2f call, inside unsafe_atan2f_impl:
- std::abs(x): 1 FABS, std::abs(y): 1 FABS (×2 each for the two uses = but compiler reuses, so 2 FABS total)
- (abs(x) - abs(y)): 1 FSUB
- (abs(x) + abs(y)): 1 FADD
- division: 1 FDIV (which on GPU expands to ~4 FP32 ops: MUFU.RCP + FMUL + FFMA + FFMA approximately)
- conditional negate of r if x<0: 1 FNEG (conditional)
- selecting pi4f or pi34f: 0 FP ops (just a select)
- angle += approx_atan2f_P<D>(r): 1 FADD
- conditional negate of angle: 1 FNEG (conditional)
- The safe_atan2f wrapper has the (y==0)&(x==0) check which involves 2 float comparisons but no FP arithmetic (it's a select on x).

For approx_atan2f_P per degree:
- Degree 3: x*(...+x*x*...) = 1 MUL (x*x) + 1 FMA (coeff + x*x*coeff) + 1 MUL (outer x*) = but more precisely: x * (c0 + x*x*c1) = x*x (1 MUL), x*x*c1 (1 MUL), c0 + prev (1 ADD), x * prev (1 MUL) = 3 MUL + 1 ADD = 4 ops. Or with FMA: 2 FMA + 1 MUL ≈ 3-5 ops. Let me count conservatively as source ops.
- Degree 3: z=x*x (not here, inline): x*(c0 + x*x*c1) = 1 MUL(x*x), 1 MUL(x*x*c1) or FMA, 1 ADD, 1 MUL = 4 FP32 ops
- Degree 5: z=x*x(1), x*(c0 + z*(c1 + z*c2)) = inner: z*c2(1), c1+prev(1), z*prev(1), c0+prev(1), x*prev(1) = 5 + 1(z) = 6
- Degree 7: z=x*x(1), x*(c0+z*(c1+z*(c2+z*c3))) = 1+7 = 8
- Degree 9: z=x*x(1), depth 4 polynomial = 1+9 = 10
- Degree 11: z=x*x(1), depth 5 = 1+11 = 12
- Degree 13: z=x*x(1), depth 6 = 1+13 = 14
- Degree 15: z=x*x(1), depth 7 = 1+15 = 16

Per call of unsafe_atan2f_impl (excluding polynomial): 2 FABS + 1 FSUB + 1 FADD + 1 FDIV + 1 FNEG(conditional) + 1 FADD(angle+=) + 1 FNEG(conditional) = ~8 FP32 ops (counting FABS, FNEG as FP ops, and FDIV as 1 source-level op).

Actually, let me reconsider FDIV. At source level it's 1 op. But on GPU hardware, FDIV typically compiles to MUFU.RCP + FMUL (fast path) or more ops. I'll count source-level: 1 FDIV = 1 FP32 op at source level.

Per safe_atan2f call: 8 ops (impl overhead) + polynomial ops.
Polynomial ops: 4+6+8+10+12+14+16 = 70
Impl overhead: 7 calls × 8 = 56
Sum of 7 results: 6 adds

Total per thread: 70 + 56 + 6 = 132 FP32 ops

Total: 10,000,000 × 132 = 1,320,000,000 FP32 ops.

However, the compiler will likely optimize: abs values computed once and reused across all 7 calls since vy and vx are the same. But each call still needs its own division since r depends on the same values... actually all 7 calls use the same vx, vy so the compiler could compute abs(vx), abs(vy), the division, and the conditional negate of r just once. That would reduce overhead significantly. But conservatively counting as written in source: 132 per thread.

Adjusting: 10,000,000 × 132 = 1,320,000,000.

records.kernel_demangled_name: compute_s(int, const float *, const float *, short *)

prediction.gridSz_explanation: From main(), the target kernel compute_s is launched in the third benchmark section with dim3 grids(n/256+1) and dim3 blocks(256). With command-line n=10,000,000, integer division gives 10,000,000/256 = 39,062, so the first compute_s invocation uses grid.x = 39,063 and block.x = 256.
prediction.blockSz_explanation: The host code explicitly sets dim3 blocks(256) before any launches and reuses it for compute_s. SASS also shows a standard 1D thread index computation using SR_TID.X and SR_CTAID.X, confirming a 1D launch.
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation: Per active thread, SASS shows 2 FP32 adds to form abs sums/differences, one MUFU.RCP, 5 FFMA refinement/quotient operations for r=(|x|-|y|)/(|x|+|y|), then the four atan-short polynomial evaluations: degree 3 uses 1 FMUL + 1 FFMA + 1 FMUL = 3 FLOPs, degree 5 uses 1 FMUL + 2 FFMA + 1 FMUL = 4, degree 7 uses 1 FMUL + 3 FFMA + 1 FMUL = 5, degree 9 uses 1 FMUL + 4 FFMA + 1 FMUL = 6. Counting each FFMA as 2 FLOPs and MUFU.RCP as 1 FLOP gives 13 FLOPs for the shared r computation + (4+6+8+10)=28 FLOPs for the four polynomials, totaling 41 FP32 FLOPs per active thread; with n=10,000,000 active threads on the first invocation, that is 410,000,000 FP32 FLOPs. The rare divide slowpath visible in SASS is only taken for exceptional inputs, and host initialization makes x,y positive in roughly [1.57,2.57], so it is not expected on the first invocation.
prediction.fp64_flop_explanation: Neither source nor SASS shows any double-precision arithmetic in compute_s; all arithmetic is performed in float and then converted/truncated to integer/short as needed. Therefore the first invocation executes no FP64 FLOPs.
prediction.fp16_flop_explanation: SASS contains two executed HFMA2.MMA instructions used for constant materialization/setup on the taken path, and the instructions execute once per active thread before the polynomial evaluation. Each HFMA2 performs two half2 fused multiply-adds, i.e. 4 FP16 FLOPs per instruction, so 2 instructions × 4 = 8 FP16 FLOPs per active thread; over 10,000,000 active threads this gives 80,000,000 FP16 FLOPs.
prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation: Each active thread loads x[i] and y[i] once via two LDG.E 32-bit global loads, so source/SASS imply 8 bytes of input per active thread. The unique input footprint is 10,000,000 floats from each array = 40 MB + 40 MB = 80 MB, which exceeds the 50 MB L2, so these streaming loads should be counted as DRAM reads for the first invocation.
prediction.dram_bytes_written_explanation: Each active thread stores one short result via STG.E.U16, for a unique output footprint of 10,000,000 × 2 = 20 MB. Because this first invocation writes only 20 MB and there are no reads of ds within the kernel, the written footprint fits within the 50 MB L2 and can remain dirty in L2 without eviction during the kernel, so DRAM write traffic during the invocation is best estimated as zero.

records.kernel_demangled_name: compute_i(int, const float *, const float *, int *)

prediction.blockSz_explanation: blocks is set to dim3(256), so block size is (256, 1, 1).
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation:
The kernel compute_i calls unsafe_atan2i for degrees 3,5,7,9,11,13,15 and sums the 7 results. Each unsafe_atan2i_impl computes: 4 fabsf (4 FP32 ops), 1 subtract, 1 add, 1 divide (1 FP32 op counted as 1, though hardware may expand), 1 conditional negate of r (1 op), then the polynomial evaluation, then an int cast, and conditional negate of angle.

For the polynomial part per degree:
- Degree 3: z=x*x (1 mul), x*(a + z*b) = 2 muls + 1 add = 3 ops. Total poly: 4 FP32.
- Degree 5: z=x*x (1), x*(a + z*(b + z*c)) = 3 muls + 2 adds = 5 ops. Total poly: 6.
- Degree 7: z=x*x (1), x*(a + z*(b + z*(c + z*d))) = 4 muls + 3 adds = 7 ops. Total poly: 8.
- Degree 9: z=x*x (1), 5 muls + 4 adds = 9 ops. Total poly: 10.
- Degree 11: z=x*x (1), 6 muls + 5 adds = 11 ops. Total poly: 12.
- Degree 13: z=x*x (1), 7 muls + 6 adds = 13 ops. Total poly: 14.
- Degree 15: same as degree 13 (the template specialization for 15 has the same body as 13): 14.

Common part per call (before polynomial): fabsf(x) (1), fabsf(y) (1), fabsf(x)-fabsf(y) (1 sub), fabsf(x)+fabsf(y) (1 add), division (1 div), conditional negate r (1 op if x<0). That's about 6 FP32 ops. But fabsf may or may not count - on GPU it's typically a bit operation, not a FLOP. Let me count conservatively: abs is typically not a FLOP on GPU (it's a bit mask). So common part: subtract (1), add (1), divide (1), conditional negate (1 op for negation when taken, but on average ~half take it; however we count all threads). The negate of r is conditional - for threads where x<0, there's 1 negate. Let's count it as 1 op per call on average (it's a branch, but the negate itself is 1 FP32 op when executed). Actually, the compiler likely uses predicated instructions, so the negate executes for all threads but is predicated. Let me count it as 1 FP32 op per call.

So per call: 4 common FP32 ops (sub, add, div, conditional negate) + polynomial ops.

Per thread, 7 calls:
- Call deg3: 4 + 4 = 8
- Call deg5: 4 + 6 = 10
- Call deg7: 4 + 8 = 12
- Call deg9: 4 + 10 = 14
- Call deg11: 4 + 12 = 16
- Call deg13: 4 + 14 = 18
- Call deg15: 4 + 14 = 18

Sum of 7 calls: 8+10+12+14+16+18+18 = 96
Plus 6 additions to sum the 7 results: 96 + 6 = 102 FP32 ops per thread.

Active threads: 39063 * 256 = 9,999,168 but only 10,000,000 are valid. Wait, 39063*256 = 9,999,168 < 10,000,000. Actually 10000000/256 = 39062.5, so 39062+1 = 39063. 39063*256 = 10,000,128. Threads with i < 10,000,000 execute: 10,000,000. Remaining 128 threads return early.

Total FP32 = 10,000,000 * 102 = 1,020,000,000.

prediction.fp16_flop_explanation: No half-precision operations are present in the kernel source. The compiler may insert a small number of HFMA2 instructions for constant materialization on Ampere, but without SASS confirmation, we conservatively estimate 0 FP16 FLOPs.
prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation: Each active thread reads x[i] and y[i], both float (4 bytes each). Total unique read footprint = 10,000,000 * 4 * 2 = 80,000,000 bytes = ~76.3 MB. The L2 cache is 6 MB, so the 80 MB input data does not fit in L2 and must be read from DRAM. With 128-byte cache lines and streaming access, DRAM reads ≈ 80,000,000 bytes.

With command-line args `n=10000000` and `repeat=100`, host code sets `dim3 blocks(256)` and `dim3 grids(n / 256 + 1) = 39062`, so the first compute_i launch uses grid (39062,1,1) and block (256,1,1).
metrics_explanations.blockSz_explanation: The block size is explicitly constructed as `dim3 blocks(256)` immediately before the kernel launches and is unchanged before the first compute_i invocation. Therefore the target kernel launches 256 threads per block in 1D.
metrics_explanations.fp32_flop_explanation: Each active thread loads `vx=x[i]` and `vy=y[i]`, then evaluates 7 calls to `unsafe_atan2i<DEGREE>`. Per call, source-level FP32 arithmetic is: `abs(x)-abs(y)` (1 sub), `abs(x)+abs(y)` (1 add), divide by sum (1 div), optional sign flip `r=-r` (count 1 unary neg), polynomial with degree 3/5/7/9/11/13/15 costing 4/6/8/10/12/14/14 FLOPs respectively (`z=x*x` plus Horner mul/adds and outer multiply by x), and final float-to-int conversion path is not counted as FP32 FLOPs; summing gives 8,10,12,14,16,18,18 FLOPs plus 4 common ops = actually 8/10/12/14/16/18/18 total per call including ratio/sign work, for 96 FP32 FLOPs per active thread across 7 calls. The kernel launches 39062*256=10000128 threads but only the first `n=10000000` are active due to `if (i >= n) return;`, so total FP32 FLOPs are 96*10000000 = 960000000; this is source-level and likely undercounts hardware instructions used for division/abs lowering.
metrics_explanations.fp64_flop_explanation: The kernel body and all called device helpers operate on `float` values and integer conversions only; there is no source-level double arithmetic on the executed path of compute_i. Constants for `pi4` and `pi34` in the integer variant are compile-time integer constants, so no FP64 work is executed at runtime.
metrics_explanations.fp16_flop_explanation: No half-precision variables or arithmetic appear in compute_i or its callees, and there is no evidence from source that packed FP16 helper instructions are intentionally used. Without SASS, the defensible estimate for executed FP16 FLOPs on the first invocation is zero.
metrics_explanations.dram_bytes_read_explanation: Each active thread reads one `float` from `y[i]` and one `float` from `x[i]`, for 8 bytes/thread. The accessed input footprint is `2 * n * 4 = 80,000,000` bytes over contiguous arrays, far larger than the 5 MB L2, and there is no intra-kernel reuse because each element is read once, so DRAM read traffic is well-approximated by this streaming footprint.
metrics_explanations.dram_bytes_written_explanation: Each active thread writes one `int` result `r[i]`, so the unique output footprint is `n * 4 = 40,000,000` bytes. Because this 40 MB write footprint greatly exceeds the 5 MB L2 and is streamed once, dirty lines will be evicted during the kernel, so a defensible estimate is that essentially the full output footprint reaches DRAM during the first invocation.
